content: [{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Cloud VPN: Virtual Private Network in Google Cloud (GCP)"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Cloud VPN allows you to securely connect your on-premises network to your Virtual Private Cloud (VPC) network through an IPsec VPN connection. This enables hybrid cloud scenarios where resources can reside both on-premises and in Google Cloud, communicating securely as if they were on the same private network."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"Types of Cloud VPN"},{"order":4,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Classic VPN: Supports static routing (route-based VPN) and policy-based VPN. It's the original Cloud VPN offering."},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"HA VPN: A high-availability VPN solution that provides a higher SLA (Service Level Agreement) and is recommended for production environments. It automatically configures two VPN gateways for redundancy."},{"order":6,"type":"subheading","text":"Key Concepts"},{"order":7,"type":"bullet_point","text":"VPN Gateway: A resource in Google Cloud that represents the endpoint for the VPN connection. It handles encryption and decryption of traffic."},{"order":8,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Tunnel: A secure connection between the VPN gateway and your peer VPN gateway (on-premises). Traffic is encrypted and encapsulated within the tunnel."},{"order":9,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Router (Cloud Router): Manages dynamic routing using BGP (Border Gateway Protocol) to exchange routes between your VPC network and your on-premises network. Required for HA VPN and recommended for Classic VPN."},{"order":10,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Peer VPN Gateway: Represents the on-premises VPN device. You configure the Google Cloud VPN gateway to connect to this peer gateway."},{"order":11,"type":"subheading","text":"Setting up Cloud VPN (HA VPN Example)"},{"order":12,"type":"paragraph","text":"This example outlines the steps for setting up HA VPN. Classic VPN setup is similar but involves manual configuration of tunnels and static routes."},{"order":13,"type":"subheading","text":"Step 1: Create a VPC Network"},{"order":14,"type":"code","text":"gcloud compute networks create my-vpc --subnet-mode custom"},{"order":15,"type":"code","text":"gcloud compute networks subnets create my-subnet --network my-vpc --range 10.10.10.0/24 --region us-central1"},{"order":16,"type":"subheading","text":"Step 2: Create HA VPN Gateway"},{"order":17,"type":"code","text":"gcloud compute vpn-gateways create ha-vpn-gw --network my-vpc --region us-central1"},{"order":18,"type":"paragraph","text":"This command creates the HA VPN gateway. Note down the external IP addresses assigned to the two interfaces (interface 0 and interface 1)."},{"order":19,"type":"subheading","text":"Step 3: Create Cloud Router"},{"order":20,"type":"code","text":"gcloud compute routers create my-router --network my-vpc --region us-central1 --asn 65001"},{"order":21,"type":"subheading","text":"Step 4: Create VPN Tunnels"},{"order":22,"type":"code","text":"gcloud compute vpn-tunnels create tunnel-0 --router my-router --region us-central1 --peer-external-gateway ha-vpn-gw --interface 0 --peer-ip <PEER_VPN_IP_ADDRESS_0> --shared-secret <SHARED_SECRET>"},{"order":23,"type":"code","text":"gcloud compute vpn-tunnels create tunnel-1 --router my-router --region us-central1 --peer-external-gateway ha-vpn-gw --interface 1 --peer-ip <PEER_VPN_IP_ADDRESS_1> --shared-secret <SHARED_SECRET>"},{"order":24,"type":"paragraph","text":"Replace <PEER_VPN_IP_ADDRESS_0> and <PEER_VPN_IP_ADDRESS_1> with the external IP addresses of your on-premises VPN device's interfaces. Replace <SHARED_SECRET> with a strong, randomly generated shared secret.  Ensure the shared secret is the same on both the Google Cloud VPN gateway and your on-premises VPN device."},{"order":25,"type":"subheading","text":"Step 5: Configure BGP Sessions"},{"order":26,"type":"code","text":"gcloud compute router-bgp-peers create bgp-peer-0 --router my-router --region us-central1 --peer-asn 65002 --ip-address 169.254.1.1 --peer-ip-address <ON_PREM_BGP_IP_0> --interface tunnel-0"},{"order":27,"type":"code","text":"gcloud compute router-bgp-peers create bgp-peer-1 --router my-router --region us-central1 --peer-asn 65002 --ip-address 169.254.2.1 --peer-ip-address <ON_PREM_BGP_IP_1> --interface tunnel-1"},{"order":28,"type":"paragraph","text":"Replace <ON_PREM_BGP_IP_0> and <ON_PREM_BGP_IP_1> with the BGP IP addresses of your on-premises VPN device's interfaces. The IP addresses 169.254.1.1 and 169.254.2.1 are link-local addresses used for BGP peering.  Choose unused addresses within the 169.254.0.0/16 range."},{"order":29,"type":"subheading","text":"Step 6: Configure On-Premises VPN Device"},{"order":30,"type":"paragraph","text":"Configure your on-premises VPN device to connect to the Google Cloud VPN gateway. You'll need to configure the following:"},{"order":31,"type":"bullet_point","text":"IPsec settings (IKE version, encryption algorithms, hash algorithms, etc.) - ensure these match the Google Cloud VPN configuration."},{"order":32,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Shared secret (must match the shared secret configured in Google Cloud)."},{"order":33,"type":"bullet_point","text":"BGP settings (ASN, BGP IP addresses, advertised routes)."},{"order":34,"type":"subheading","text":"Step 7: Verify the Connection"},{"order":35,"type":"paragraph","text":"Check the status of the VPN tunnels in the Google Cloud Console. Verify that BGP sessions are established and routes are being exchanged. You can also test connectivity by pinging resources in your VPC network from your on-premises network, and vice versa."},{"order":36,"type":"subheading","text":"Important Considerations"},{"order":37,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Firewall Rules: Ensure that firewall rules allow traffic between your on-premises network and your VPC network."},{"order":38,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Routing: Configure appropriate routes to direct traffic between your networks.  Cloud Router automates this for HA VPN."},{"order":39,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Security: Use strong shared secrets and regularly rotate them. Consider using Cloud KMS to manage your shared secrets."},{"order":40,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Monitoring: Monitor the health and performance of your VPN tunnels using Cloud Monitoring."},{"order":41,"type":"subheading","text":"Troubleshooting"},{"order":42,"type":"bullet_point","text":"VPN tunnel status: Check the status of the VPN tunnels in the Google Cloud Console. Look for errors or warnings."},{"order":43,"type":"bullet_point","text":"BGP session status: Verify that BGP sessions are established and routes are being exchanged. Use the 'gcloud compute routers get-status' command."},{"order":44,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Firewall rules: Ensure that firewall rules are not blocking traffic."},{"order":45,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Connectivity tests: Use ping or traceroute to test connectivity between your networks."}]
